title: Dreams and Visions of the Night
lead: In the Bible God sometimes speaks through dreams: to Abimelech, Jacob, Joseph, Pharaoh, Solomon, Nebuchadnezzar, Daniel, and to Joseph and the Magi in Matthew. Some dreams are plain; others need interpretation, which the Bible insists belongs to God. The Law and prophets also warn against false dreamers (Deuteronomy 13:1–5; Jeremiah 23:25–32).

sections.b: Genesis is full of dreams: God warns Abimelech (20:3), Jacob sees the stairway (28:12) and Laban is warned (31:24). Joseph's story has three pairs of dreams (37; 40; 41). Numbers 12:6 says God speaks to prophets in dreams but to Moses "mouth to mouth." Solomon receives wisdom in a dream (1 Kings 3:5), Daniel interprets Nebuchadnezzar's dreams (Daniel 2; 4), and Joel promises that "your old men will dream dreams" (Joel 2:28; Acts 2:17). Matthew's birth story turns on five dreams (Matthew 1:20; 2:12, 13, 19, 22), and its Joseph, like the patriarch Joseph, is a dreamer who goes down to Egypt (Matthew 2:13–15); and Pilate's wife suffers in a dream (Matthew 27:19). Jeremiah warns against prophets who "tell their dreams" in place of God's word (Jeremiah 23:28).
